title: Systems: Epidemics, Percolation & Phase Transitions
description: Between hosts, an infection is a reproduction number. Above R = 1 it spreads through a population; below it, it dies out; a phase transition, the same as water freezing or a fluid percolating through porous rock. Unlocks the Contagion Network Map.

puzzle.goal: A population of N is split into the susceptible S, the infected I and the recovered. Infected hosts meet others at random and transmit at a rate β per contact with a susceptible; they recover at a rate γ and die of other causes at a rate μ. Write how the number of infected changes.
puzzle.name: Kermack–McKendrick SIR model with vital dynamics, the infected equation
puzzle.form: β * S * I / N - ( γ + μ ) * I
puzzle.ask: At the start S ≈ N, and the infection grows only if R₀ = β/(γ + μ) is above 1, a phase transition. It stops spreading once a fraction 1 − 1/R₀ is immune. Find that herd-immunity threshold.
puzzle.method: New infections come from S·I contacts, a fraction I/N of each susceptible's meetings; infected leave by recovery or death.
